g.text: File-tree — delivery, refresh-before-open, and expansion-scoped watch
[the file is inside a git repository]
sidebar shows one controlled tree per project
[collapse / ancestor collapse / Files unmount / project removal]
close watcher when last owner leaves
[another window still owns the same scope]
an extras-less refresh never wipes them)
a diff INSIDE the root gets
the described repository is in Files
where main unlinks the stdin spill. On-disk extras
persist — *Remove from Files* takes the project away.
Every local open sends a tree — a git root when there is one,
else the containing directory as a
`send-tree!` is reached, so they synthesize nothing.
Containment therefore only ever removes synthetic roots: a repo
nested inside a browsed directory stays its own project.
A synthetic root covered by another does not duplicate it — its
walked subtree is re-based and merged in, so the file you just
opened is always in the tree (the `--others` invariant).
A filter may force known paths open, but a direct-click scope that
is still refreshing remains closed until its reply commits.
Removal is manual — project header ⟶ *Remove from Files*.
